extracted.intended_audience: researchers applying to USDA NIFA (especially AFRI) competitive grants and peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and review guidance for competitive USDA NIFA proposals (with specific AFRI review criteria), covering scoring scale, scientific and programmatic criteria, application requirements, and panel summary expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard Adjectival Rating Scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation criteria are aligned to scores of: Excellent, Very Good, Good, Fair, Poor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the adjectival ratings to map evaluative judgments of proposal quality to standard score categories (Excellent → Poor). No additional numeric conversion provided on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality, novelty, and significance of the proposed research; conceptual adequacy and clarity of the project; potential for scientific advancement of the field; appropriateness of the experimental design and methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the project is novel and significant, clearly and conceptually sound, likely to advance the field, and whether the experimental design and methods are appropriate to achieve the aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications of Project Personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifications, training, and experience of the PI and team; adequacy of facilities and resources; time committed to the project; past productivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the project team’s expertise and track record, whether institutional resources and facilities are adequate, and whether personnel have sufficient committed effort to carry out the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to Program Priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of the topic for agriculture; alignment with USDA mission and program priorities; contribution to mission needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge how well the proposal addresses priority topics and USDA/NIFA program goals and whether it meaningfully contributes to stated mission needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Plan/Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Soundness of the project plan; feasibility of timeline; risk mitigation; stakeholder engagement (where relevant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the plan is logically organized and feasible, timelines are realistic, potential risks are identified with mitigation strategies, and stakeholders are engaged appropriately when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes and Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Expected products and outputs; anticipated outcomes for stakeholders; long-term impact on agricultural systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the clarity and significance of expected deliverables, benefits to end-users or stakeholders, and likely long-term effects on agricultural systems and practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Applications (RFA) Required Contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The RFA includes: program purpose and legislative mandates; award types; eligibility requirements; evaluation criteria; submission instructions; program goals and funding priorities; proposal submission deadlines; application submission instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing or reviewing proposals, ensure compliance with all RFA-specified elements (eligibility, submission instructions, deadlines, stated priorities and goals) as these drive whether proposals are acceptable and how they will be evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel Summary Document
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'panel summary' document is written by a panel member reflecting the panel consensus and detailing the salient points of the panel's assessment of strengths and weaknesses; contains a synthesis comments section describing areas for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel summaries should synthesize reviewer consensus, clearly state major strengths and weaknesses, and provide constructive improvement suggestions; these summaries inform final rankings and applicant feedback.
